mismatch.cMessage: What do you want to remove? [pq or ?*]

summary: At evaluated commit e7623b67450936e27add7de87567f83f84ed1190, terrain-transitions matches 57/137 screens, leaving 80. The fresh single-case diagnostic at bd4fb5b6a0a6197472855e6c3bcc3ddedbcf4cd0 stops at step 57, key "R" (remove), before dispatch: the JS command-admission seam rejects it because “remove” is absent from ADMITTED_COMMANDS. C cmd.c:1820-1821 binds R to do_wear.c:doremring(), whose C screen is “What do you want to remove? [pq or ?*]”. Thus the first source owner is the remove command path in do_wear.c, not trap.c:float_down(); float_down() remains a downstream dependency after Ring_off() is reached. The evaluated and diagnostic commits differ only in GOALS.json and scripts/dodown.test.mjs; game JavaScript is identical.

source.branch: The exact stop is before dispatch of the capital-R remove command. nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1820-1821 binds R to doremring(). do_wear.c:doremring() (1872-1890) counts worn equipment; if none, prints “Not wearing any accessories or armor.” and returns ECMD_OK; otherwise it prompts through getobj("remove", remove_ok, GETOBJ_NOFLAGS) when accessories are not unique, paranoid removal is enabled, or a canned command exists; cancel returns ECMD_CANCEL; success returns armor_or_accessory_off(otmp). The saved case has one levitation ring, but C still enters getobj because armor and accessory counts make the choice prompt active; C shows “What do you want to remove? [pq or ?*]”. The source-family work needed to complete this end-to-end path is doremring(), remove_ok(), armor_or_accessory_off(), select_off(), and Ring_off()/Ring_off_or_gone(), with the current function bodies compared whole and their active production callers wired. Current JS rejects at cmd.js admitParsedCommand() because ADMITTED_COMMANDS omits remove and has no doremring dispatch. The downstream ring branch then calls trap.c:float_down(0,0), which is a separate source-file dependency and the next known blocker after Ring_off() is wired.
callers: cmd.c command table row 1820-1821: key R, command name remove, function doremring. This is the direct production caller and C renders “What do you want to remove? [pq or ?*]” at the stop. The JS binding resolves R to remove, but js/cmd.js admitParsedCommand() throws UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError because remove is absent from ADMITTED_COMMANDS; there is no doremring command dispatch in the JS path.

do_wear.c doremring() 1872-1890 calls count_worn_stuff(), getobj("remove", remove_ok, GETOBJ_NOFLAGS), and armor_or_accessory_off(). Current JS has count_worn_stuff() and getobj(), but no remove_ok wrapper or doremring() command path.
do_wear.c remove_ok() 3458-3465 calls equip_ok(obj, TRUE, TRUE) as getobj’s callback. js/do_wear.js equip_ok() exists; remove_ok() is not wired as a callback.

do_wear.c armor_or_accessory_off() 1771-1829 calls select_off(), then Ring_off() for a selected ring. js/do_wear.js armor_or_accessory_off() is present but its ring/accessory dispatch remains fail-closed.
do_wear.c select_off() 2696-2821 validates cursed/inaccessible equipment and sets takeoff.mask. js/do_wear.js select_off() currently throws at its ring checks, before Ring_off().

do_wear.c Ring_off_or_gone() 1347-1446 handles RIN_LEVITATION by calling float_down(0,0); Ring_off() 1449-1452 dispatches with gone=false. js/do_wear.js Ring_off_or_gone() still refuses the levitation-ring arm.
dependencies: cmd.c command binding/dispatch must admit “remove” only when its matching JS handler is wired; the current admission refusal is a port boundary, not C behavior.
count_worn_stuff() is already implemented in js/do_wear.js and returns the equivalent counts and default item together.
getobj() is already implemented in js/invent.js; its remove_ok callback needs to preserve the C GETOBJ_SUGGEST, GETOBJ_DOWNPLAY and GETOBJ_EXCLUDE_INACCESS outcomes from equip_ok().
equip_ok() is implemented in js/do_wear.js. remove_ok() is a small source wrapper over equip_ok(obj, true, true).
armor_or_accessory_off() and select_off() are existing partial JS implementations and must finish the whole C functions for an ordinary worn ring selection.

Ring_off_or_gone()/Ring_off() are existing partial JS implementations. The levitation-ring path reaches trap.c float_down(0,0); its current JS owner only supports the W_SADDLE branch. This is downstream of the exact step-57 command-admission stop.

evidence: Saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260925173439-v1.json at e7623b67450936e27add7de87567f83f84ed1190 reports terrain-transitions 57/137 screens, 2784/3811 RNG calls and 57/137 cursors; 80 screens remain.

Single-case diagnostic .cache/synthetic-scans/v1/terrain-transitions.json at bd4fb5b6a0a6197472855e6c3bcc3ddedbcf4cd0 reports screensEmitted=57, commandRefusal=true, key="R", command=remove, keyCursor=command; C top line: “What do you want to remove? [pq or ?*]”. The diagnostic replay input SHA is 019af0a80e7b54489f621844c9f11640ee021eb5315d0b009ba464688402f45e.

nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1820-1821 binds R to command “remove” and function doremring(). This verifies the direct C owner of the step-57 command path; the scanner boundary is the JS admission list, not C behavior.

nethack-c/upstream/src/do_wear.c:doremring() (1872-1890), remove_ok() (3458-3465), armor_or_accessory_off() (1771-1829), select_off() (2696-2821), and Ring_off_or_gone() (1347-1446) were source-traced as the whole source call chain; Ring_off() (1449-1452) is its entry wrapper.

js/cmd.js:admitParsedCommand() (1903-1915) rejects commands absent from ADMITTED_COMMANDS; “remove” is absent. The command table maps the key correctly, but there is no doremring dispatch. js/do_wear.js has count_worn_stuff(), equip_ok(), armor_or_accessory_off(), select_off(), and Ring_off_or_gone() partial implementations; the ring path has named refusals.

The recorded C steps around the downstream levitation path show `R` at 57, `q` at 58, then a C message “You float gently to the stairs.” at step 59. This supports float_down as a later dependency but does not make it the first mismatch owner.

The diagnostic replay commit bd4fb5b6a0a6197472855e6c3bcc3ddedbcf4cd0 differs from evaluated commit e7623b67450936e27add7de87567f83f84ed1190 only in GOALS.json and scripts/dodown.test.mjs (verified by git diff --name-only); JavaScript game files are identical. B2 source reservations do not overlap do_wear.c or these JS callers.

active: Capital-R remove command: cmd.c command-table R row dispatches doremring(); the admitted synthetic case reaches this command at step 57 and C displays the remove selection prompt.
blocked: The JS replay currently rejects “remove” in cmd.js admitParsedCommand() before dispatch because the command is absent from ADMITTED_COMMANDS.

After admission, the JS source path still lacks doremring()/remove_ok() and has partial armor_or_accessory_off()/select_off()/Ring_off_or_gone() implementations; the selected levitation ring later reaches trap.c float_down().
